title: Revenue Management Standard: Rent Increases for Existing Vehicle, RV & Boat Parking Agreement Tenants
content:
The company may raise a Vehicle, RV & Boat Parking Agreement tenant's rent with an existing-customer rate increase notice, on the following terms. The month and day figures referred to are those of the space class (first-increase wait, interval, caps, loyalty tenure and notice period).

**1. Timing of a notice.** An increase notice may be sent only when the handling date is not earlier than the start date plus the first-increase wait of the class. An increase notice may also be sent only when the handling date is not earlier than the last rent change date plus the interval of the class. Months are calendar months counted to the same day of the later month, or that month's last day when the day does not exist. Both comparisons are inclusive: the notice may go on the day the count lands.

**2. Standing.** The former rule that increase notices go only to agreements in active status is **no longer in force** in its former wording; it has been superseded by a restated standing requirement.

**3. Size of an increase.** The cap on one increase is the standard increase cap of the class, as a share of the current monthly rent; it is replaced by the loyalty increase cap when the tenant's tenure on the agreement, in whole calendar months from the start date to the notice date, is at least the loyalty tenure. The two caps never combine, and at or past the loyalty tenure the loyalty cap is the one that applies. Where the street-rate ceiling applies to the class, the new rent also may not exceed the space's posted street rate on the notice date, and an agreement already at or above that street rate gets no increase. The new rent is the lower of these limits, rounded down to the cent.

**4. Prepaid rent.** While a prepaid rent plan in active status covers the agreement, no increase notice is sent and no increase takes effect before the prepaid term ends.

**5. Effective date and notice period.** The effective date is the first rent due date at least the notice period of the class in calendar days after the notice date. The new rent is applied only when the handling date is not earlier than the notice date plus the notice period. Notice days are counted as calendar days starting the day after the notice date.

**6. Defective notices.** An increase notice that breaks any of these rules is defective: it is rescinded in full with an increase-rescinded change whose new rent equals the previous rent, and the rescission does not count as a rent change for the interval rule. Rescission of a defective increase follows the class setting that defective increases are rescinded in full.

### Boundary cases (hypothetical dates)

- First-increase wait of 9 months, start date 15 March: a notice may go on 15 December; on 14 December it may not. With a start date of 31 May, 9 months lands on 28 February (29 February in a leap year).
- Notice period of 30 days, notice dated 1 May: days are counted from 2 May, the 30th day is 31 May; the new rent may be applied on 31 May and not on 30 May, and the effective date is the first due date falling on or after 31 May.

### Worked limit (hypothetical figures)

Current rent $200.00 on a class with a 10% standard cap and a 5% loyalty cap at 36 months; street rate on the notice date $214.50.
- Tenure 20 months: the cap gives $220.00, the street rate gives $214.50; the new rent is at most $214.50.
- Tenure 36 months: the cap gives $210.00, below the street rate; the new rent is at most $210.00.
- Street rate $195.00: the agreement is already above it and gets no increase.

superseded_clauses: Increase notices go only to agreements in active status.
